name: Armodafinil
lead: Armodafinil is the R-enantiomer of modafinil and a prescription wakefulness-promoting medication. The US label lists it to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness associated with obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy or shift work disorder, and specifies that in sleep apnea it treats sleepiness and not the underlying obstruction [10]. Grokipedia gives the brand name as Nuvigil and a 2007 US approval [1].

As with modafinil, the label says the mechanism of wake promotion is unknown, with properties similar to modafinil in animal and in vitro tests [10]. A 2012 study found the R-enantiomer to be a dopamine uptake inhibitor with properties that may differ from the racemic mixture [3].

Armodafinil is mentioned in looksmaxxing communities mainly in comparison with modafinil as a study and productivity aid. No published trial has tested it for any appearance outcome, and the available looksmax.org material about it is limited to passing comparisons.

paras: The label indications are excessive sleepiness in obstructive sleep apnea (alongside continuing treatment such as CPAP), narcolepsy and shift work disorder [10]. The American Academy of Sleep Medicine's 2021 guideline on central disorders of hypersomnolence and a 2021 review of sleepiness in sleep apnea discuss wake-promoting drugs within wider treatment pathways [2][4].

Off-label investigation has included bipolar and unipolar depression and schizophrenia; a meta-analysis of modafinil augmentation in depression covered modafinil and related agents [8]. Registered trials have tested armodafinil as an add-on in schizophrenia [11][12].

The label lists serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) or multi-organ hypersensitivity, angioedema and anaphylaxis, persistent sleepiness, psychiatric symptoms, effects on driving and machinery, and cardiovascular events [10]. As with modafinil, the label notes reports of intrauterine growth restriction and spontaneous abortion in pregnancy [10].

The label describes the R- and S-enantiomers of modafinil as having similar pharmacological actions in animals [10]. Grokipedia states armodafinil has a longer plasma half-life than the racemic mixture [1], and a 2012 paper reported that the R-enantiomer inhibits dopamine uptake at the dopamine transporter and is of interest in stimulant-abuse research [3]. A registered PET study examined armodafinil's dopaminergic activity in healthy adults [14].

A 12-week double-blind study of 196 adults with narcolepsy compared two armodafinil doses with placebo on objective and subjective sleepiness measures [5]. A separate 12-week placebo-controlled study enrolled adults with sleep apnea who still had sleepiness despite CPAP [6], and another reported effects on wakefulness and memory in sleep apnea [7].

Registered trials have studied armodafinil as adjunctive therapy in schizophrenia, for sleepiness after traumatic brain injury, for fatigue in multiple sclerosis, and in simulated driving in healthy volunteers [11][12][13][15][16]. No studies were found of armodafinil for appearance outcomes.

Armodafinil is prescription-only in the US [10]. On looksmax.org it appears chiefly in discussions of modafinil, where one user reported anxiety and sweating on armodafinil and preferred modafinil [9].

timeline.event: A phase 3 armodafinil trial in narcolepsy begins [17].

card.summary: The longer-acting R-enantiomer of modafinil, prescribed for sleepiness; no appearance effect has been studied.
card.note: Prescription-only in the US; label warns of serious rash and hypersensitivity reactions.

quick.overview:
Armodafinil is the R-enantiomer of modafinil, approved in the US for excessive sleepiness in narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work disorder. In looksmaxxing forums it comes up mostly as an alternative to modafinil for staying alert.

No trial has tested it for appearance, and forum material on it is thin.
quick.mechanism: The label says the mechanism is unknown and similar to modafinil. Research reports it inhibits dopamine reuptake at the dopamine transporter.
quick.risks: The label warns of serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hypersensitivity, psychiatric symptoms and cardiovascular events. It is prescription-only in the US.
